newsitem.title: USA: Cardinal comfortable with earnings estimates.
newsitem.headline: Cardinal comfortable with earnings estimates.

text.p: Cardinal Health Inc President John Kane on Thursday said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus estimates for the company's earnings in the fourth quarter, the current fiscal year and fiscal 1998.
Analysts on average estimate the company will earn $0.55 in the fourth quarter of 1997, $2.02 in the full year, and $2.45 in fiscal 1998, according to First Call.
Those estimates exclude merger-related charges in 1997, and represent earnings growth rates in excess of Cardinal's stated objective of 20 percent, he said.

He also said that revenues in the current fourth quarter are expected to be at the lower end of the company's longer-term growth range. The company has chosen not to accept less profitable customers, he said, and it also exited one piece of business that did not provide sufficient returns.
Earlier in the day, the stock was downgraded by Morgan Stanley to outperform from strong buy.
Cardinal, one of the leading U.S. pharmaceutical service providers, was among the most actively traded stock on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday. It fell 2 to close at 58.

Kane also said the company was positioned to continue its history of generating revenues faster than the pharmaceutical wholesale industry's average. He expects internal revenue growth of 15 percent to 20 percent in an industry expected to grow at between 10 percent and 12 percent.
